questions.prompt: What is revenue?

choices.text: Money earned from customers before costs
Money borrowed from a bank loan
Money left after paying every expense
Money sitting in the bank right now

questions.correct_answer: Money earned from customers before costs
questions.intro: Three words get mixed up. REVENUE (sales) is all the money earned from customers before costs. PROFIT is revenue minus all expenses for the same period. CASH is the money actually in the bank right now. They can differ: a business can have revenue but no profit if costs are high; it can show a profit but little cash if customers have not paid yet or if money went into inventory. Watching all three tells the real story.

questions.prompt: The stand's revenue is what?
questions.intro: A lemonade stand sells 30 cups at 1 dollar: revenue is 30 dollars. Lemons, sugar and cups cost 18 dollars: profit is 30 - 18 = 12 dollars. But if a neighbor bought 5 cups and promised to pay tomorrow, the cash box has only 25 dollars from sales today. Revenue is what you sold, profit is what is left after costs, and cash is what is in the box.
